one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Check 1 asks for more than the expect line says. PASS requires `good.port === 9000`, which is a test that valid JSON still parses. The line "catches the JSON.parse error and returns {} instead" doesn't force that. PASS also requires the exact output `{} {"port":9000}`. Check 2 is also stricter than "npm test passes". PASS requires the summary to read `# fail 0`, which is exact runner-specific wording, and FAIL includes "reports zero tests run". All of these stricter tests should be under Advisory, not in the PASS/FAIL conditions.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the six tracked files and the scripts in package.json. The builder brief only runs `npm test`, which maps to `node --test`, and test/config.test.js exists for it to find. The files it edits (src/config.js, test/config.test.js, README.md) all exist. The verifier's Check 1 is valid shell: mktemp/printf write the temp files, the double-quoted JS contains no `$`, and `echo "exit=$?"` reports node's exit status. With `node -e`, process.argv[1] and [2] are the two extra arguments, so the paths are read correctly. The JS is valid, and `--input-type=module` with `import { loadConfig } from './src/config.js'` resolves against the repository root. This works whether config.js is ESM or uses CJS named exports. Check 2 runs `npm test`, which exists. Every command would run as written.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. Item 1: the verifier's Advisory section, which sits outside PASS/FAIL, says "after this change `node src/app.js <bad file>` starts with defaults" rather than printing `bad config`. It also says "the prescribed {} return hides the error", while the issue wants users told which file is broken. Builder step 5 flags the same tension in a note. Item 2: builder step 2 says to replace the existing 'bad JSON throws' test in test/config.test.js with one where bad JSON returns a value deepEqual to {}. It ties this to step 4, which requires `npm test` to pass. Item 3: verifier Check 1 writes `{port: 9000` to a file and calls loadConfig on it. It PASSes when the output is `{}` with no SyntaxError and the exit code is 0. It also checks that a valid file still parses, which goes beyond the item but doesn't conflict with it.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items, and neither item is broken. Item 1: Check 1's PASS condition asks only that the bad file returns `{}` with no SyntaxError, that valid JSON still parses (`good.port === 9000`) and that the code catches the parse error. The valid-JSON part is a regression guard, not an extra demand on the error path. Nothing asks for the file name, the line or a warning. The file-and-line tension appears only under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)". Item 2: the builder brief says to catch the error "and returns {} (a new empty object)". On the issue's wish for file-and-line detail, it says "Do not add behaviour beyond the acceptance lines to resolve this; just flag it for the reviewer". It never asks for a clearer thrown error. The warning against swallowing missing-file errors covers a different error, so it doesn't change what happens on a parse error.

methods-private.why: Not met: the builder brief includes one of the verifier's probes. Builder step 2 says to test that "loadConfig on a file containing `{port: 9000` returns a value deepEqual to {}". Verifier Check 1 uses that same input (`printf '{port: 9000'`) and passes only if the result is `{}`. That is a set of inputs with expected outputs shared by both briefs, which the criterion forbids. Asking the builder to write its own tests is allowed, but handing it the checker's exact case is not. The rest holds: running `npm test` is allowed because an expect line names it, and the builder brief has no PASS or FAIL wording and no grep.
